original_claim: Sparse coupling rises while dense coupling falls, widening the sparse-minus-dense gap.
corrected_wording: On fixed_source/all_expert inputs and the common four-cell population, sparse Pearson coupling rises in every condition while matched dense coupling falls; the paired gap widens in all ten.
metric: Pearson raw router projection score vs signed mean post-GELU activation
reference: Same source-final dense hidden vectors across sparse and dense
population: 128 positions per expert; common valid population is 128 layer-expert units
limitations: Five source seeds; descriptive only, not causal.

original_claim: The extension coupling values are a separate sparse-native n=128 result.
corrected_wording: The quoted changes reproduce fixed_source/all_expert coupling. “Sparse-native n=128” is a reporting-label error: 128 means token positions per all-expert unit, not layer-expert units. The expert-output n=128 table contains both fixed_source and native modes and is a different metric family.
metric: Coupling Pearson vs expert-output relative error/cosine
probe_mode: fixed_source/all_expert; output table modes remain separate
limitations: Original reports preserved; only generator and figure labels corrected.

original_claim: Sparse/dense geometry diverges consistently during recovery at both sparsities.
corrected_wording: Centered output CKA on fixed_source inputs decreases from step 0 to 5000 in all seeds at both sparsities, nonmonotonically. On dense_native inputs it increases from 0 to 5000 in all seeds, then generally falls from its step-2500 high point. Universal divergence is unsupported.
metric: Centered output CKA; other geometry metrics/ranks separately available
reference: Same-step dense expert; dense_native inputs move across steps
population: 2048 validation positions; per expert then equal layer aggregation
limitations: CKA is similarity; moving-reference and fixed-input results answer different questions.

original_claim: Fixed-gate distortion is 3-8x larger at 5000 than at 2500.
corrected_wording: For fixed_source inputs with same-step dense gates, equal-layer mean per-layer squared-error ratios rise for every seed from 2500 to 5000. D and reference energy are both changing; ratio of aggregate energies differs from mean layer ratios.
metric: Squared aggregate distortion D, reference energy, layer ratios, aggregate ratios
reference: Same-step dense moving gates; fixed-source-final gates separate
population: 2048 probe positions, full and accepted-only populations
limitations: Ratio is squared; numerator/denominator changes do not establish movement away from fixed geometry.

original_claim: The IMP mask retains no more gradient energy than random, with excess at most .004 everywhere.
corrected_wording: Task-gradient excess is near null for fc1/.80, but small positive excess occurs for fc2 at both sparsities and fc1/.85; all five seeds in those groups exceed the ten-draw null range. Auxiliary gradients lack random controls. No equivalence claim is tested.
metric: Task/aux gradient energy, exact-count random null, cosine; subspace overlaps separately
probe_mode: Native dense/sparse states on common minibatch identities
reference: Same-step dense; identical training-loader batch indices
population: 16 seen training batches; complete dense tensor denominator
limitations: Training data not held out; ten random draws; no practical equivalence threshold.

original_claim: fc1 keep fraction around .328 contradicts nominal .80 sparsity.
corrected_wording: Nominal budget is allocated jointly per expert across concatenated fc1+fc2 weights; individual tensor keep fractions vary. Combined keep is .2000008 at .80 and .1499996 at .85.
population: 4 layers x 32 experts x two matrices
limitations: Overall expert-weight sparsity differs from full-model sparsity; biases unpruned.

original_claim: Magnitude-based selection preserves function at the state that selected the mask.
corrected_wording: Only the two measured C-to-D transitions are supported: .7902848->.80 removes about 4.63% of remaining weights with near-zero probe CE changes; .80->.85 removes 25.00% and raises probe CE. The increments differ.
metric: C/D mask counts, paired CE and KL(C||D)
probe_mode: Direct selection-state C -> isolated masked D
reference: Same validation probe and precision; router fixed, native assignments recomputed
limitations: Do not interpret unequal pruning increments as a target-sparsity-only effect.

original_claim: Sparse models can match dense validation performance despite substantial measured expert-function and native-gradient differences.
corrected_wording: Four conditions strictly match same-seed dense CE at 5000 attempted steps. Their measured output geometry and task-gradient cosines are shown numerically; this is descriptive co-occurrence, not causality. “Substantial” has no predefined threshold.
metric: Strict CE labels, expert output CKA/error, task-gradient cosine
reference: Same-seed dense control; same-step dense experts
population: Four matching conditions; 2048 validation positions and 16 seen training batches
limitations: Training gradients not held out; states/representations/routing differ; no generalization beyond cohort.
